designVerdict: SELECTED - the two channel load switches, 2 per board
notes: 60 V, 30 A, 23 mOhm @10V Vgs, TO-252. At the full 5 A bus current that is 0.58 W, comfortable in a TO-252 with a copper pour.
Vgs(th) 1.6 V, Qg 68 nC @10V. The high Qg is helpful here rather than a drawback: the gate RC that sets the inrush ramp wants a slow turn-on.

Chosen over the alternatives on dissipation. AOD407 (C6396162) is 68 mOhm = 1.70 W and has far better stock (42k vs 2.5k) if this one runs out. MOT1793G (C7495206) is 100 V but 85 mOhm = 2.13 W. SI7489DP (C499484) is 100 V and 41 mOhm but $4.38.

60 V gives 1.67x margin on a 36 V bus. It does NOT leave room for a future 48 V/240 W bus - that would want the 100 V part. Judged acceptable because 48 V requires respinning every module anyway (the XL1509 is a 40 V part), so the door is not one this FET closes.
FOUND VIA the jlcpcb MCP parametric search. The keyword-only search had led to the $4.38 SI7489 - 10x the price and 3x the dissipation of this part.
Fallback if stock runs short: AOD407 (C6396162), 42k stock, 68 mOhm. Fine for the channel switches at 2.43 A (0.40 W); hotter but workable on the main path (1.70 W).

60 V vs 100 V RESOLVED in favour of this part, on thermals: 0.58 W against the 100 V MOT1793G's 2.13 W, which the iPhone-16 size target makes awkward. An earlier body-diode argument was also offered and is RETRACTED - it does not hold for input-side surges (Q1 off, bus discharged, diode reverse-biased). The TVS concern is instead removed by using SMAJ36CA (Vc 58.1 V) rather than SMAJ40CA (Vc ~64 V).

TWO per board, not three. The master pass FET between VBUS and the bus was REMOVED: it was the source of all three gate-network faults (ramp on the wrong node, 180 s turn-off, dV/dt self-turn-on during the PD 5->36 V step), and the channel switches already shed every load it could. VBUS now connects straight to the bus.

Gate network per switch: R_pu 100k gate-to-source, R_pd 100k to the 2N7002 drain, BZT52C12 clamp, 3.3 uF gate-to-drain. Gives a 0.99 s ramp, 0.12 A inrush into 3.3 mF, 567 us turn-off and 2.16 W average during the ramp. The switches close after the bus is static at 36 V, so there is no source dV/dt to reject.
